claims.title: Local hidden-law deviations compose into a finite-horizon sequential coupling bound
claims.scope: two finite hidden-law models connected by one detailed-to-abstract state map, common source-symbol and signal alphabets, action-independent transitions and observations, and finite horizon T
assumptions: initial abstract-state laws differ by at most epsilon_0 in total variation
matched detailed and abstract states have observation-row TV at most epsilon_o
matched detailed states and abstract states have abstract next-state TV at most epsilon_K
maximal couplings are applied conditionally while histories remain matched
nonclaims: the product coupling bound is sufficient and need not be tight
the theorem does not cover action-dependent hidden dynamics or observation channels

claims.title: Approximate hidden-law coupling bounds transfer uniformly to optimal no-signal and noisy-observation coding values
claims.scope: finite-horizon Bayesian zero-error prefix coding over one common complete bounded codebook universe and common signal-history policy interface
assumptions: every matched-state codebook stage cost differs by at most epsilon_c
every cumulative policy cost lies between zero and the declared finite-horizon cost ceiling M_T
the same deterministic or exogenously randomized policy mapping is admissible in both models
nonclaims: the value theorem does not cover unrestricted policies observing detailed internal state identity
safe model-specific codebook pruning does not alter the common-universe optimum but is not itself the coupling theorem

claims.title: Expected clairvoyant path-oracle and Bayes-regret differences inherit approximate quotient bounds
claims.scope: the same finite code-sequence comparator class evaluated under detailed and abstract hidden-law paths
assumptions: on matched abstract-state paths every fixed code sequence has stage-cost difference at most T epsilon_c and identical switch cost
transition-only coupling controls abstract path divergence
Bayes regret is policy value minus expected path-oracle value
nonclaims: the regret bound is a triangle-inequality upper bound and may exhibit cancellation in practice
the path oracle remains a retrospective benchmark rather than a causal policy

claims.title: The approximate quotient theorem collapses to zero value loss at exact bisimulation
claims.scope: an abstraction whose initial block law, codebook stage costs, observation rows, and abstract transition rows match exactly
assumptions: all local deviations epsilon_0, epsilon_c, epsilon_o, and epsilon_K are zero
nonclaims: zero local deviation is an exact model statement rather than a claim about empirical equality
the boundary result does not convert quotient-state count into physical memory

claims.title: Representative two-state abstraction has certified positive but bounded value loss
claims.scope: the declared three-state rational example merging states zero and one while their source, observation, and abstract transition laws differ by at most 1/20 TV
assumptions: the first state in each block supplies the representative abstract parameters
the complete K3 zero-error prefix-codebook family and declared finite horizon are used
nonclaims: the representative abstraction is not asserted to minimize the certified bound
the numerical deviations are instance specific

claims.title: Bounded exact approximate-hidden-law deviation and value audit
claims.scope: the rational detailed and abstract models, codebooks, paths, values, regrets, and finite-horizon coupling expressions exercised by the repository tests
assumptions: all configured hidden-path, codebook, partition, and prefix-shape caps complete without truncation
Python Fraction arithmetic is used for every finite deviation and cost calculation
nonclaims: bounded exact checks are not a scalability theorem
a small internal value-loss bound is not evidence that reality is simulated
